# The `Verified` gate's `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.11)` cell hangs after ~99% of the suite and is cancelled at the 60-minute job timeout

## Symptom

The cell prints progress normally for ~10 minutes, reaches `[ 99%]` with **zero** `F`/`E`
markers, and then emits nothing at all until GitHub kills it:

    2026-08-07T17:04:16.9396830Z ....................................... [ 99%]
    2026-08-07T17:55:12.0420609Z ##[error]The operation was canceled.

`timeout-minutes: 60` is set on the `test` job in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`.
The CI bot reads the cancellation as a failure and votes `Verified -1` + `Code-Review -1`,
so an otherwise-green change cannot land.

## Not change-specific

Seen on at least two unrelated changes on 2026-08-07:

* change 1505 (`9fb3`), three consecutive runs — 31194624887, 31199714760, 31206898501 —
  including one run **after** a rebase onto `origin/main` @ 9532650f24.
* run 31208164115, a different change, same signature: `[ 99%]` then
  `The operation was canceled.`

The other matrix cells (ubuntu py3.12, ubuntu py3.13, macos py3.13) complete the same
selection in 11-21 minutes on those same runs, so it is specific to the ubuntu/py3.11 cell.

Counting the progress dots on run 31199714760's cell: 11160 of ~11215 tests had reported
before the silence, so roughly the last ~55 tests are where it stalls. It is a hang in the
test tail, not in coverage combining or teardown after the run.

## Does not reproduce locally

On macOS with the CI-faithful configuration — `uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra
reviewbot --extra ui --python 3.11`, then `REBAR_REQUIRE_EXTRAS=1 pytest -m "not
integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q -p no:cacheprovider --durations=25
--cov=rebar` — the suite finishes in 15:00 with 11196 passed, 19 skipped, exit 0. So the
trigger involves the Linux runner (4 vCPU, `fcntl.flock`-backed store locking) rather than
the interpreter version alone.

## Why it matters

Every change in flight can be blocked by a red `Verified` that reflects no real defect, and
the only workaround is to keep posting `recheck` until a run happens to get through. That is
the same class of problem as a gating advisory failure: the gate stops discriminating.

## Suggested first moves

- Add `-v` (or `--timeout` via `pytest-timeout`) to the ubuntu cells so the hanging test
  names itself instead of being invisible behind `-q` dots.
- Suspect first the store's write-lock paths (`fcntl.flock` + `mkdir`) and any test that
  shells out to `rebar` as a subprocess, since a blocked lock acquire is the shape that
  produces exactly this silence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [operator-attested] the hanging test (or the blocking call) is named, with a CI log line or a local
      reproduction showing it stalled
- [x] [operator-attested] the ubuntu py3.11 cell completes within the 60-minute job timeout on three
      consecutive Verified runs
- [x] whatever makes the hang diagnosable (a per-test timeout, `-v`, or a faulthandler
      dump) is committed, so a recurrence names itself instead of going silent
